body.name: Projected nested-cell and Gaussian-grid implementation handle
body.construction: Use \(P_B\) to generate feasible nets and use exactly the coordinate order, lexicographic child order, parent-only recursion, and closed-boundary convention fixed by \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). At depth \(k+1\), evaluate the uniform approximation test only on the nonempty feasible parts of the closed dyadic children of the unique ambient box selected at depth \(k\), retain every such child whose approximated cell value is within the prescribed vanishing tolerance of the approximated minimum over those siblings, and select the lexicographically first retained child. If a boundary point belongs to several retained closed children, treat all of them as eligible and apply that same lexicographic rule; never compare or select an unrelated cell. The empirical feasible cells are therefore a nested sequence of nonempty closed cells, because the sibling attaining the finite approximated minimum is always retained, and their ambient dyadic diameters tend to zero. Couple the resulting singleton-targeted \(\widehat r_n\) to \(\widetilde\theta_n\) and to a rectangle-constant Gaussian minimax rule whose state, observation, and integration meshes refine slowly enough for the conditional normal-approximation error to vanish.
